failure_summary.description: Calls were often present, but an endpoint, field, or value did not match the requested operation or its constraints.
Explicit filters or qualifiers were omitted, placed in the wrong parameter slot, or lost in malformed call objects.

patch.reasoning: Most failures were not missing whole requests; they came from mapping the request to the wrong endpoint or schema fields, and from losing constraints in the final call objects. The rules focus on those errors without repeating general call-coverage advice.

edits.target: (No learned rules yet. Rules will be added through the reflection process.)
edits.content:
## Map requests to tool schemas
- Compare candidate endpoints by the exact operation and all requested qualifiers. Prefer an endpoint that supports the full request, not one that matches only its broad topic.
- Map each constraint to the field that represents it. Distinguish quantities from repetitions, and operation-specific values from ordinary search terms. Use the endpoint’s documented canonical values and parameter types; follow its required/optional classification exactly.
- Include supported optional parameters needed to express explicit constraints. For constrained random draws or searches, encode the requested value rather than silently using an unconstrained default; use an unrestricted value only when the user leaves that dimension open and the schema calls for one.

## Preserve call structure
- Represent each tool call as its own JSON object with exactly the keys required by the answer format. Do not combine separate calls or repeat keys inside an object.
- Before submitting, check that every requested qualifier appears in the appropriate call and parameter slot.
